4  THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER
The petitioners in both petitions are, the husband and his family members.

They are before this Court calling in question registration of a crime in Crime No.278/2022, pending before the I Additional Civil Judge (Jr. Dn.) and JMFC Court, Magadi, Ramanagar District, for the offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 415, 149 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Page No.5 is retyped and replaced vide chamber order dated 24.01.2025 NC: 2024:KHC:51591 2.

Learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for respondent No.2 in unison submit that the parties to the lis were before the concerned Court in Crl.Misc.No.151/2022 under the provisions of the Domestic Violence Act, 2006, and during the pendency of the that proceedings, the parties have settled the dispute among themselves amicably and decided to live together.
They have also filed memorandum of settlement under Section 89 read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005.

An application Section 320(2) r/w. 482 of the Cr.P.C.,
seeking permission to compound the afore-quoted offences before this Court to that effect.
One of the conditions of the settlement recognizes the closure of the present proceedings.

3. The affidavit filed by the parties to the lis along with the application, reads as follows:
"4.

The Petitioners and the Respondent No.2 further submitted that, in view of the settlement of issues between the parties the Respondent No.2 agreed to re-union with the Petitioner No.1/husband to lead a happy matrimonial life.

5. The Petitioners and the Respondent No.2 requests the same before the Learned Magistrate in Criminal Misc. No. 151/2022 and the learned Magistrate Page No.6 is retyped and replaced vide chamber order dated 24.01.2025 NC: 2024:KHC:51591 refer the same to Mediation Centre,
Bengaluru and the same settlement reported before the Mediation and the Memorandum of settlement under Sec. 89 r/w Rule 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules 2005, in view of the settlement, both the parties agreed to with the cases filed against each other.

6. The Petitioners and Respondent No.2 further submitted that the Respondent No.2 agreed to co- operate with Petitioners to quash/closure of Claim No.278/2022 pending on the file of the 1st Addl.
Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC at Magadi for the offences punishable under Sec. 498(A), 323, 504,
506, 415, r/w Sec. 149 of IPC and under Sec. 3 and 4 of D.P. Act.
In view of the same, the Respondent No.2 have no objection to quash FIR in Crime No. 278/2022 of Kudur Police Station.

They further submitted that the alleged offence under Sec. 498(A) of IPC is non compoundable in nature and hence, they prays this Hon'ble court to accord permission to compound the offence in view of the comprise arrive between the parties, hence, this application for kind consideration of this Hon'ble Court."

In the light of the afore-quoted affidavit of the parties and the fact that the dispute between them is amicably settled and are living together happily, though the offences alleged against the petitioners in the case at hand inter alia is one punishable under Section 498A of the IPC, I deem it appropriate to accept the application and permit them to compound the offences, as the allegations are not against the State.
Page No.7 is retyped and replaced vide chamber order dated 24.01.2025 NC: 2024:KHC:51591 4.

For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The criminal petitions are disposed.

(ii) The impugned Crime No.278/2022 in both the petitions, pending before the I Additional Civil Judge (Jr. Dn.) and JMFC Court, Magadi, Ramanagar District,
stands quashed.

Sd/-
